Frontend architecture report · Nuvina D2C storefront · small store edition

A lean, scalable Shopify storefront for Nuvina

An audit of the current Next.js repository, a recovery of the product page deleted from its history, and a folder structure sized for a small ecommerce site. Visitors browse products, add them to a cart and pay through Shopify's own checkout. The structure stays simple now and has a clear path to grow later.

Repositorynuvina-figma-landing-page · main · 3 commits
Referencefeature-reputation/webui (Endless Domains)
DesignFigma nuvina · nodes 1:3771 and 1:4505
Revised25 September 2026

01Summary and sizing

Today the repository is a single landing page. All fourteen components sit together in components/home/, and every piece of content lives in one hardcoded file. There is no Shopify connection, no product route and no cart. The first commit had a product page for HYDRATE, which was later deleted. Its breakdown into sections was sound, but it was hardwired to that one product.

Nuvina does not need the scale of the Endless Domains webui. There are no user dashboards, wallets or domain management tools, and Shopify handles checkout, payments, orders and customer accounts. The frontend has four jobs: show the brand, show the products, keep a cart, and hand the visitor to Shopify checkout. The structure below is built for exactly that. It uses a few folders grouped by purpose, one file per component, a single lib/shopify folder for all store access, and no global state library.

What "small scale" means here. Roughly 5 to 30 products, about six page types, one or two developers, product content edited in Shopify admin, checkout and accounts on Shopify, and India only with INR pricing. If any of these change a lot, section 14 explains how the structure grows without a rewrite.

6page types to build
3top level folders in src
about 40component files in total
10blocks shared by home and product designs
3 to 4 weeksfor one developer

03The deleted products/hydrate page

9ddeb2e · Initial Commit

This commit contains app/(main)/products/hydrate/page.tsx, a shared (main)/layout.tsx, 13 components in components/product/, 5 in components/ui/, 3 in components/layout/, plus lib/data.ts and lib/format.ts.

8710ea2 · remove extra pages

Deletes the hydrate route and the shared layout. The product components are left behind with nothing using them.

33595c6 · update to the latest package

Deletes the product, ui and layout components and the data files in the same commit as the Next, React and Tailwind upgrade.

The page composed Breadcrumb, ProductGallery, ProductInfo, sticky ProductTabs, KeyBenefits, WhatsInsideProduct, NutritionFacts, HowToUse, WhyItWorks, RealPeopleResults, CustomerReviews, CompleteRoutineProduct and FAQSection. Most of these have a direct match in the new Figma product page.

Why it could not grow

The folder name, the find(p => p.slug === "hydrate")! lookup, the metadata and the components all pointed at one product. ProductInfo read the global hydrateProduct object instead of taking props. "Add to Cart" only changed a label with a timer. Pack sizes were hand typed rather than Shopify variants.

What to keep

Keep the section breakdown, the layout pattern (header and footer in a route group layout), StarRating, ProductCard, and formatINR, which becomes formatMoney. A single products/[handle] route with the same sections, fed by Shopify, replaces the whole folder.

04What to borrow from Endless Domains, and what to skip

The webui is a large Pages Router application with 40 routes, 20 services, 13 Redux slices and about 200 component folders across component/, template/ and design-system/. That scale fits a product with dashboards, wallets and many flows. Nuvina is a catalogue with a cart, so it takes the ideas, not the size.

Endless hasNuvina usesWhy
design-system/{primitives, composites, layouts} with barrel filescomponents/{ui, layout, sections, home, product, cart}, no barrelsGrouping by purpose still gives order. Plain imports are simpler and build faster.
One folder per component with index.ts and .module.scssOne file per component, styled with TailwindWith about 40 components, folders per component would double the file count for no gain.
core/services, core/enum, core/model, api/, config/lib/shopify/ (client, queries, types, functions)There is one data source, so one folder holds all of it.
Redux store with 13 slicesA small CartProvider context for the drawer; the cart itself lives in ShopifyServer components read the cart from Shopify, and server actions change it.
styles/tokens.scss and breakpoint mixinsTokens in the Tailwind @theme in globals.cssSame idea, one place, fewer files.
Layout owning SEO and cart bootstrappingThe (shop)/layout.tsx plus generateMetadataKeep this pattern. It is the right one.
ESLint with import sorting, Prettier, HuskyESLint and Prettier with the same import sort groupsWorth copying. Husky can wait until a second developer joins.
_archive/, backup/, legacy component/ and template/NothingGit history is the archive. Avoid having two places for the same kind of file.

What was left out on purpose

A /cart page is not needed, because the drawer is the cart and its checkout button goes straight to Shopify. There are no account pages either, since the account icon links to Shopify's hosted customer accounts. There is no Redux, no barrel files, no hooks or types folders, and no mock data layer. If a hook is only used by one component, it stays in that file. If lib/utils.ts passes 200 lines, split it then.

07Rules and naming

Six rules keep a small codebase tidy as it grows.

  1. Pages fetch, components display. Only files in app/ and lib/actions.ts call lib/shopify. Components receive data as props.
  2. Put a file where it is used. Use ui for generic pieces, layout for every page, sections for two or more pages, and home or product for one page. When a home component starts being used on the product page, move it to sections.
  3. Keep the browser part small. Components are server components by default. When one needs state, move only that piece into its own file with "use client", the way MostLovedTabs.tsx sits next to MostLoved.tsx.
  4. Tokens only. Colors, fonts and widths come from globals.css. Components never contain hex values or max-w-[…].
  5. Put content where the editor lives. Anything about a specific product goes in Shopify. Brand copy that rarely changes goes in lib/content.ts. Nothing is typed directly into a component.
  6. No new folders without a reason. A new top level folder needs a line in CLAUDE.md explaining why.
ThingConventionExample
Component filePascalCase, named export, props type in the same fileProductCard.tsx exporting ProductCard and ProductCardProps
Client pieceParent name plus what it doesMostLovedTabs.tsx, GalleryViewer.tsx
Data functionStarts with get, named after the Shopify objectgetProduct, getCollectionProducts
Server actionVerb firstaddToCart, removeCartLine
TokenNamed by role--color-brand, --color-ink, --color-goal-hydration

08Shopify connection

The frontend talks to the Shopify Storefront API from the server. The token never reaches the browser. The flow for a visitor looks like this:

BrowseServer pages call getProduct()→ AddaddToCart() server action→ CartShopify cart id in a cookie→ PayRedirect to cart.checkoutUrl→ OrderShopify handles payment, COD, email 
# .env.example
SHOPIFY_STORE_DOMAIN=nuvina.myshopify.com
SHOPIFY_STOREFRONT_TOKEN=          # server only, never NEXT_PUBLIC_
SHOPIFY_API_VERSION=2026-07
SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET=
NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL=https://www.nuvina.in
NEXT_PUBLIC_WHATSAPP_NUMBER=

lib/shopify/client.ts

import 'server-only'

export async function shopifyFetch<T>(query: string, variables?: object, tags?: string[]): Promise<T> {
  const res = await fetch(
    `https://${process.env.SHOPIFY_STORE_DOMAIN}/api/${process.env.SHOPIFY_API_VERSION}/graphql.json`,
    {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        'X-Shopify-Storefront-Access-Token': process.env.SHOPIFY_STOREFRONT_TOKEN!,
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({ query, variables }),
      ...(tags ? { next: { tags } } : { cache: 'no-store' }),
    },
  )
  const json = await res.json()
  if (!res.ok || json.errors) throw new Error(json.errors?.[0]?.message ?? `Shopify ${res.status}`)
  return json.data
}

lib/shopify/index.ts

export async function getProduct(handle: string): Promise<Product | null> {
  const data = await shopifyFetch<{ product: RawProduct | null }>(PRODUCT_QUERY, { handle }, ['products'])
  return data.product ? toProduct(data.product) : null   // flattens edges, parses JSON metafields
}

The product route that replaces products/hydrate

// src/app/(shop)/products/[handle]/page.tsx
type Props = { params: Promise<{ handle: string }> }

export async function generateMetadata({ params }: Props) {
  const product = await getProduct((await params).handle)
  return product ? { title: product.seo.title, description: product.seo.description } : {}
}

export default async function ProductPage({ params }: Props) {
  const product = await getProduct((await params).handle)
  if (!product) notFound()
  const related = await getRecommendations(product.id)

  return (
    <>
      <Container className="grid gap-10 lg:grid-cols-2">
        <ProductGallery images={product.images} />
        <ProductInfo product={product} />
      </Container>
      <TrustStrip items={trust} />
      <HealthGoals goals={healthGoals} />
      {product.labReportUrl && <LabTests href={product.labReportUrl} />}
      <KeyBenefits items={product.keyBenefits} />
      <RitualTimeline title="How to use?" steps={product.ritual} />
      <Ingredients items={product.ingredients} />
      <WhatMakesItBetter items={product.freeFrom} />
      <MostLoved bestSellers={related} />
      <Reels items={reels} />
      <Testimonials items={testimonials} />
      <Faq items={product.faqs} />
    </>
  )
}

Here trust, healthGoals, reels and testimonials come from lib/content.ts. Adding a new product is done entirely in Shopify admin, with no code change.

Cart in one file

// src/lib/actions.ts
'use server'
export async function addToCart(variantId: string, quantity = 1) {
  const jar = await cookies()
  let cartId = jar.get('cartId')?.value
  if (!cartId) {
    cartId = (await createCart()).id
    jar.set('cartId', cartId, { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: 'lax', path: '/' })
  }
  await addCartLines(cartId, [{ merchandiseId: variantId, quantity }])
  revalidatePath('/', 'layout')                 // header count and drawer refresh
}

AddToCartButton calls this inside useTransition to show a pending state, then opens the drawer through CartProvider. That context only holds whether the drawer is open. The drawer's checkout button is a plain link to cart.checkoutUrl.

Keeping pages fresh

Add one webhook in Shopify admin for product and collection updates, pointing to /api/revalidate. The route checks the HMAC signature and calls revalidateTag('products', 'max'). Prices and stock then update within seconds, while pages stay static and fast.

09Where each piece of content lives

A small store needs only a few custom fields. Use Shopify's standard fields wherever they exist, add about eight product metafields, and keep brand copy in one TypeScript file until the marketing team asks to edit it themselves.

Why JSON metafields. Timelines, ingredients and FAQs are small lists of objects. A JSON metafield holds each one in a single field, and one parse function reads it. If editors find JSON awkward later, move that one field to a metaobject. Only the parse function changes.

Use next/image for all Shopify images and give the hero image and first gallery image priority. Load fonts through next/font. For carousels, use CSS scroll snap through the existing scroller hook instead of a slider library.

12Roadmap

This is the short version. The companion Nuvina Build Playbook has the prompts and checklists for each phase.

P0 · Documents and setup

1 day

Write CLAUDE.md, SCOPE, FIGMA_MAP, SHOPIFY_SETUP and PLAN. Set up the Claude Code settings.

P1 · Clean up and foundation

2 days

Remove the junk files, move to src/, turn on strict mode, add ESLint and Prettier, rename the tokens and load fonts.

Done when lint and build pass and the home page looks unchanged.

P2 · Shopify store and data layer

2 days

Set up a development store with the five products, variants, metafields, collections and menus. Build lib/shopify.

Done when getProduct('hydrate') returns typed data.

P3 · UI and layout components

3 days

Build the ui/ files, the (shop)/layout.tsx, and the header and footer with Shopify menus.

P4 · Home page

4 days

Build the shared sections and home only blocks, compose the page from Shopify and content.ts, and delete the old folders.

P5 · Product page

4 days

Build products/[handle], the gallery, the variant picker synced to the URL, and the product sections.

P6 · Cart and checkout

2 days

Build the server actions, drawer, header count and handoff to Shopify checkout.

Done when a test order goes through on the development store.

P7 · Remaining pages, QA and launch

3 days

Build collections, search and policy pages, the sitemap and metadata, the webhook, a responsive and accessibility pass, Lighthouse checks and deployment.

PrettierWith prettier-plugin-tailwindcss
CIOne GitHub Actions job: install, lint, typecheck, build
HostingVercel, which handles caching and revalidation with no setup
TestsA single Playwright smoke test (home loads, add to cart, checkout link) before launch
LaterHusky, GraphQL codegen and a component preview page, once a second developer joins

14When to grow the structure

The structure is small on purpose, but every folder maps onto a larger one, so growing is a matter of moving files rather than rewriting them.

SignalNext step
components/ passes about 60 files, or one folder passes 15Give that folder subfolders, or move to Endless style tiers: ui becomes primitives, sections, home and product become composites, and layout becomes layouts
lib/shopify/queries.ts passes about 400 linesSplit it into queries/product.ts, queries/collection.ts and so on, and add GraphQL codegen
Marketing wants to edit reels, testimonials or health goalsMove them from content.ts to Shopify metaobjects
Subscriptions, bundles builder, quiz or loyaltyAdd src/features/<name>/ holding that feature's components, actions and logic together
More countries or currenciesAdd Shopify Markets, and pass @inContext(country) in the queries
Three or more developersAdd Husky, codegen, a component preview route and lint rules for import boundaries
